name: Group 6 Bergama shared palette

method.space: OKLab (Ottosson 2020); straight-line mix, t = 0 board, t = 1 image colour; out-of-gamut colours lose chroma at constant lightness and hue
method.pairing: same family, same lightness rank inside the family; board neutrals with the grey of the same lightness; ink, road and street kept

ramp_rule.note: mean OKLCH ratios to the roof of the four uses in diagram reference 2; outline chroma x1.3 is a design choice (the reference's keys: x1.6-4.8)

method.checks: CIEDE2000; Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009) dichromacy matrices at severity 1 in linear sRGB; WCAG 2 contrast ratio; working target 10 between topic colours (ours)

land_use.label: Mixed use · shop below, home above

schemes.title: What stands: building use and height
schemes.harmony: Analogous: the board's land-use family on one warm arc, plum to ochre
schemes.contrast: Contrast of hue on one warm arc; light-dark from the 3D faces
schemes.why: The boards already teach this legend, so D1 reads at a glance beside them.
schemes.note: Uses are read from the roofs; walls are tone steps of the roof's own hue. For dichromats a mixed roof and a residential lit wall are only 3.3 apart, so name uses on roofs, not walls.

topics.label: Mixed use · shop below, home above

ramp.label: Height on a plan, low to high: the board's INTENSITY path, evenly re-spaced (class breaks still to be set from the survey's floor counts)

schemes.title: Heritage and landmarks
schemes.harmony: Monochromatic: oxblood in four lightness steps
schemes.contrast: Light-dark contrast only; one hue makes heritage read as one theme
schemes.why: All else stays neutral, so the layers of the old town read as one family.
schemes.note: The zone tint is 1.3 from street grey for red-green dichromats, so the zone always carries its dashed oxblood edge. Monument roofs and sacred walls are 4.0 apart: name the monuments.

schemes.title: Movement
schemes.harmony: Greys with one hue: an achromatic hierarchy and one accent
schemes.contrast: Contrast of saturation: grey streets, one warm accent for walking
schemes.why: Width and grey value rank the network; the accent carries the walking routes along the water.
schemes.note: Lanes are the lightest void by design; edge lines carry them, as on the boards.

schemes.title: Water and green
schemes.harmony: Analogous cool: yellow-green to blue, the cold half of the set
schemes.contrast: Cold-warm contrast: the one diagram where the cool family leads, on the warm context
schemes.why: The Selinus and its planting are the subject of the brief, so here they take the colour.
schemes.note: Parks and fields are 9.2 apart for protanopes, under the target of 10, so fields keep their furrow stripes and parks their trees.

schemes.title: Services and daily life
schemes.harmony: Analogous warm arc, violet to yellow, separated by lightness
schemes.contrast: Contrast of hue and light-dark together; blue stays for water, as on the boards
schemes.why: Five unrelated services need five distinct colours; each also carries a roundel icon.
schemes.note: The two plums differ mainly in lightness; for dichromats a health roof is 2.1 from civic walls, so every service carries its roundel letter.

experiment.name: Red-yellow-blue triad: health in the water slate, civic in the dark plum
experiment.verdict: separates as well, but breaks the boards' rule that blue means water

schemes.title: Study areas
schemes.harmony: Near-triad: one colour per owner (hues 290, 50, 186) on a white casing
schemes.contrast: Hue, then light-dark: each line on its white casing over any scheme, never filled
schemes.why: Aras asked for the working areas colour-coded so they read at first glance, thicker and without curve-point markers (17 Oct, 19:19), in colours from the palette and its research (19:23). Outlines only, never filled or hatched (project rule).
schemes.note: No corner markers; each owner's name sits on white in the line colour.

method.tones: light, mid and dark are three tones of one colour; 'use' says which tone does what
method.codes: light = the zone's flat fill; mid = fill lightness - 0.17, chroma x 1.3 (cap 0.09); dark = lightness 0.42, lowered in 0.005 steps until 4.5:1 on its fill and on paper, chroma x 1.3 (cap 0.06); hue kept; heritage takes diagram D2's tones
method.fills: hues from the palette; lightness and chroma of the new fills picked with a coordinate-descent search on a 0.005 x 0.004 OKLCH grid (scratch script, not kept) that raised the smallest differences, then fixed in make_palette.py
method.targets: CIEDE2000 10 between any two fills for normal vision (as the diagrams); 7 between neighbours in the legend for the worst dichromat, matrices on linear and on encoded sRGB (ours)
